# Skill Studio for DeepSeek Harness

A Codex-compatible skill system for DSH, with a first-class page in the left
sidebar. It reads and w

rites plain `SKILL.md` folders, so the same skills work
in Codex, DSH, and the shared `.agents` dire

plain `SKILL.md` folders, so the same skills work
in Codex, DSH, and the shared `.agents` directory.
## What it does

- **One Skill page in the sidebar** — browse every Codex, DSH, and shared skill,
search it, read its

instructions, and see which copy is effective.
- **Create, edit, duplicate, delete, and restore** —

writes the Codex
`SKILL.md` format with YAML frontmatter. Deletions go to a recoverable
`.trash` fo

lder inside the same scope.
- **Enable or disable per surface** — `disable-model-invocation` control

s the
model catalog and the `skill` tool; `user-invocable` controls direct user
invocation.
- **Code

x scopes** — `~/.codex/skills` and `<project>/.codex/skills` are bridged
into DSH's skill registry,

so existing Codex skills appear in the agent
catalog without copying them.
- **Invoke in conversatio

n** — type `$skill-name` in a chat to inject the full
`<skill_content>` block into that turn, exactl

y like Codex. The existing
`/skill-name` form also keeps working.
- **Progressive disclosure** — the

model receives only names and descriptions;
full instructions load on demand through the `skill` to

ol or `$name`.
- **Codex presentation metadata** — `agents/openai.yaml` `interface` and
`policy.allo

w_implicit_invocation`, plus legacy `config.toml` `[interface]`
fields such as `displayName`, `short

Description`, `brandColor`, and
`defaultPrompt`, are shown when present.
## Scopes
| Scope | Location | Writable | Notes |

| Codex user | `~/.codex/skills` | yes | Bridged into DSH by this plugin |
| Codex project | `<proje

ct>/.codex/skills` | yes | Nearest `.git` ancestor, or the workspace directory |
| DSH user | `~/.ds

h/skills` | yes | Native DSH filesystem provider |
| DSH project | `<project>/.dsh/skills` | yes | N

ative DSH filesystem provider |
| Shared Agent | `~/.agents/skills`, `<project>/.agents/skills` | ye

s | Visible and editable when present |
| Codex built-in | `~/.codex/skills/.system` | no | Read-onl

y; duplicate into a writable scope |
| Bundled/runtime | DSH packages | no | Read-only; duplicate wh

into a writable scope |
| Bundled/runtime | DSH packages | no | Read-only; duplicate when possible |

`DSH_CODEX_HOME` (or `CODEX_HOME`) changes the Codex home; `DSH_HOME` and
`DSH_AGENTS_HOME` change t

he DSH and shared roots. The Codex home is scanned
under `<home>/skills`.

A project copy outranks a user copy; a DSH copy outranks a Codex copy of the
same name. The page mar

ks the losing copy **Shadowed** and shows both, so a
stale duplicate is never invisible.
## Skill format
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A skill is a directory bundle `<name>/SKILL.md` (recommended) or a flat
`<name>.md` file directly un

der a scope root. The only required frontmatter
fields are `name` (kebab-case) and `description`. Op

tional companion files can
live beside `SKILL.md` (`references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`, `agents/ope

nai.yaml`,
`config.toml`, `icon.svg`).

`disable-model-invocation: true` hides the skill from the model catalog and the
`skill` tool. `user-

invocable: false` removes it from the `$name` / `/name`
gesture. Both default to allowed.
## Using a skill in chat
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The skill's instructions enter the current step as a `<skill_content>` block,
and the catalog tells

the model to follow it rather than load it again. Typing
`/release-checklist` uses DSH's existing us

er-skill gesture and has the same
effect.

The model can also load any model-invocable skill with the existing `skill`
tool, which returns the
same canonical `<skill_content>` shape.
## Installation
Install directly from the public GitHub repository:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or install the release tarball:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or, after the npm release, use the package name:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Refresh the page after installation; the **Skills** icon appears in
the left panel list.
## Design notes

- The host half is plain Node ESM with only `node:` imports. It registers a
`codex-studio` provider

on `ctx.skills`, owns the authenticated
`/api/skill-studio-codex.*` routes through `ctx.connection.f

etch`, and installs
one `agent/pre-step` listener for `$name`.
- The client half is a plain-JavaScri

pt module loaded by
`window.__ModuleLoader__`; it uses only React, theme tokens, and the public
slot

/locale services.
- File writes are atomic (temp file plus rename), names are validated, and
every m

utating route is authenticated by the existing browser session.
- Deleting a skill renames its bundl

e into `<scope>/.trash/` with a sidecar
record, so **Trash → Restore** works without a database.
- T

he Codex provider invalidates its catalog on a debounced filesystem watch, so
edits made in Codex, V

S Code, or a shell reach the next model step.
- This published edition uses its own Loader row, side

bar panel id, API prefix,
locale namespace, and provider name. It can coexist with the local
`@local
/dsh-skill-studio` build instead of replacing it.
## Limits

- Editing always updates `SKILL.md` frontmatter; comments on managed keys are
not preserved when the

key is rewritten. Unknown frontmatter keys and
`metadata:` blocks are preserved.
- Renaming a skill

is intentionally not done in place: the name in `SKILL.md`
is its identity. Duplicate and delete th

e old copy instead.
- Symlinked skill bundles are visible but read-only.
- The page manages the defa

ult workspace for project scopes. Per-session
workspaces with a different cwd are still discovered b

y the model, but the
management page uses the process workspace.
